title: Advanced home search filters (price range, beds/baths, property type, amenities) on a listings page — Hearthway Realty
notes: v1 is a server-rendered BEM page: left <aside> filter form#home-search (keywords, price range, bedrooms/bathrooms selects, property-type checkbox list, amenity checkboxes wrapped in labels, HOA/days-on-market, 'Search homes'/'Reset filters') beside a results summary and six listing cards. v2 is a Next.js + Tailwind rebuild: results now come first in the DOM (flex-row-reverse), the filter form gets a regenerated id and React ':rN:' ids, fields are regrouped (home type first, keywords/HOA moved into a 'More filters' <details>, Co-op and EV charger options added, property types and amenities reordered), names move to camelCase (priceMin, bedrooms, homeType, features), the price range lives in <hw-price-range> and the amenity list ('Features') in <hw-checkbox-group>, both declarative shadow roots with labels re-pointed via for. Copy changes: 'Search homes' -> 'Show results', 'Reset filters' -> 'Clear all', 'Bedrooms' -> 'Beds', 'Min price' -> 'Minimum', 'Swimming pool' -> 'Pool', '47 homes' -> '47 results'. Decoys: a header location search whose submit now says 'Search homes', a mobile quick-filter bar (md:hidden) with legacy min_price/max_price/beds controls, hidden min_price/max_price inputs that mirror the shadow price field, an active-filter chip row (House/Townhouse/Condo), a closed mobile filters <dialog> repeating Townhouse/Pool checkboxes, '47 results', 'Clear all' and 'Show results', and a hidden saved-search modal. Listing cards are reordered, a sponsored new-construction card is inserted, and market stats move into <hw-market-stats> shadow DOM.

targets.description: Minimum price input of the price-range filter in the filter sidebar
Bedrooms ('Beds') select in the filter sidebar
'Townhouse' property-type checkbox in the filter sidebar
'Swimming pool' amenity checkbox (now 'Pool' under Features) in the filter sidebar
Submit button of the filter form ('Search homes', now 'Show results')
Result count text in the results summary ('47 homes', now '47 results')
